chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abu Hammam, who said:

I said to Al-Reza (peace be upon him): 'A man has a debt upon him, and wealth presents itself to him; should he pay off his debt or perform Hajj?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should pay off part of it and perform Hajj with part of it.' I said: 'Supposing it is not enough except for the expenditure of Hajj?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'He should pay off [the debt in] one year and perform Hajj in [another] year.' I said: '(Supposing if) the wealth is given from the Sultan (ruling authority)?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no problem upon you.'
ai.seo_question: What is the priority between paying off debt and performing Hajj in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him) clarifies that fulfilling financial obligations takes precedence over the obligatory Hajj, establishing a practical hierarchy where debt repayment is prioritized to ensure the pilgrim's spiritual state is not compromised by lingering liabilities. The ruling accommodates varying degrees of financial capacity, allowing for partial payment and partial pilgrimage if funds permit, or deferring Hajj entirely until debts are settled. This jurisprudence underscores the Shia emphasis on social justice and contractual fidelity, ensuring that the pilgrim’s journey is not undertaken while neglecting the rights of creditors.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Abu Hammam who said,

‘I said to Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, ‘A man happens to have the debt upon him, and something present itself to him, should he pay off his debt or perform Hajj?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should pay off part of it and perform Hajj with part of it’. I said, ‘Supposing it does not happen to be except a quantity for expenditure of the Hajj?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He should pay off one year, and he should perform Hajj one year’. So I said, ‘(Supposing if) the wealth is given from the Sultan (ruling authority)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem upon you’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa has narrated from abu Hammam who has said the following:

“I once asked al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who owes a debt and he earns a certain amount; if he must pay the debt or perform al-Hajj. He (the Imam) said, ‘With a certain part he pays the debt and with other part performs al-Hajj.’ I then asked, ‘What happens if it is only enough for al-Hajj?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘One year he pays the debt, and one year performs al-Hajj.’ I then asked, ‘Can an amount be received from Sultan?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful in the case of all of you.’”
